newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF to drill in Brazil by 1998 - report.
newsitem.headline: YPF to drill in Brazil by 1998 - report.

text.p: Argentina's YPF will begin to prospect and drill for oil in Brazil before the end of the year, its president Roberto Monti said.

In an interview with the new business daily BAE, Monti said in the next few months YPF and Brazil's Petrobras would open up the first of 1,500 service stations they will run jointly in both countries.
He also said YPF would take part in the tender for high-risk areas that will be launched by the governments of Argentina and England southwest of the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic.
Monti said after the acquisition of U.S. firm Maxus in 1995, the Argentine oil giant began to chart a strategy to diversify the industry's risk.
"YPF has to expand quicker than its competitors in the oil industry -- not in a rushed fashion but rather with growth that's profitable," he said.

"YPF has two central aims: to grow outside the country to lower Argentine risk, and to capture no more than 50 percent of the domestic market in order not to spark anger over alleged or possible dominant practices," he added.
Monti also said over the next five years the company would study 50 investment projects to see which was more feasible or profitable.
He predicted in the next decade YPF would aim for annual growth of 3.5 percent in oil production and 10 percent in gas production.
